blocks.text: When several threads touch the same memory, a data race must not happen. For a single number the simplest solution is an **atomic** variable: the operations are indivisible. `AtomicI64.fetch_and_add(n)` adds, `load()` reads.

For more complex data you use a **`Mutex`**: you take it with `lock()` and release it with `unlock()`. A safer way that cannot forget the unlock is **`Locked[T]`**, which puts the value inside the lock: `lock()` returns a `Guard` and the lock is released automatically when the `Guard` leaves its scope.
`Arc[T]` is counted sharing that lets several threads own the same value: `clone()` adds a new owner and the value is dropped when the last owner lets go.

blocks.q: When is the lock released when you access the value inside `Locked[T]`?
options: Automatically, when the `Guard` leaves its scope
blocks.why: Forgetting to unlock cannot happen in this design.

blocks.q: The simplest safe way to increase a single counter from several threads?
blocks.why: Atomic operations are indivisible; no data race occurs.
